title: Theorem A
body_md:
Let $\alpha\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ and $\epsilon>0$. Then
		\[
		-\log\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)\le(2+\epsilon)\,L\,\mathfrak s(P)+O(1)
		\]
		for all $P\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$ outside $\Phi^{-1}(Z)$, where $Z$ is finite. If $\Phi(\alpha)$ is real and irrational, the constant $2L$ cannot be replaced by any smaller number. In particular, for every $\mathfrak q$-reduced pair $\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $F_\alpha(\mathbf x)\neq0$ one has $|F_\alpha(\mathbf x)|\ge C\,|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{-(1+\epsilon)L}$ with $C=C(\alpha,\mathfrak q,\epsilon)>0$.
head: environment

title: Theorem B
body_md:
Assume the $abc$ conjecture. Let $\alpha\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ with $\Phi(\alpha)\notin\{[0:1],[1:0]\}$ and let $\epsilon>0$. Then
		\[
		-\log\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)\le(q_0+q_1+\epsilon)\,\mathfrak s(P)+O(1)
		\]
		for all integral points $P$ with $\Phi(P)\neq\Phi(\alpha)$. For $\mathfrak q=(2,3)$ and $\Phi(\alpha)=[1:1]$ the constant $q_0+q_1=5$ cannot be lowered, even though $2L=12$.
head: environment

title: Theorem D
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
			\item For every finite set $S\subset\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ there is a finite morphism $f\colon\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}$ with the following properties: it is unramified outside $\{0,1,\infty\}$, it satisfies $S\subset f^{-1}(\infty)$, and all its ramification indices over $0$ equal $3$ and all over $1$ equal $2$.
			\item For each form $G$ as in Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical}, the weighted $abc$ conjecture of signature $(3,2)$ implies Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} for $G$ and every coprime weight vector. Only finitely many coefficient pairs $(4e,-1)$ are needed, and they depend only on $G$.
			\item The $abc$ conjecture is equivalent to $\mathrm{wABC}(3,2;4e,-1)$ for $e\in\{1,3,9,27\}$.
			\item If Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} holds for $\mathfrak q=(2,3)$ and the four rational targets $[1:4e]$, $e\in\{1,3,9,27\}$, then it holds for all coprime weight vectors and all algebraic targets.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Theorem C
body_md: Let $F$ be as above with coefficients in $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, and assume $G$ has no repeated factors. For every $\epsilon>0$ there is $C>0$ with $|F(x,y)|\ge C\,|(x,y)|_{\mathfrak q}^{L(\kappa-2-\epsilon)}$ for all coprime $(x,y)\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $F(x,y)\neq0$. If $\kappa\ge3$, then $F(x,y)=m$ has only finitely many integral solutions for every $m\neq0$.
head: environment

label: lem:veronese
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:veronese}
		For $\mathbf x\in K^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}$ and $v\in M_K$ we have $\max_i\lVert x_i^{r_i}\rVert_v=\lVert \mathbf x\rVert_{v,\mathfrak q}^L$. Consequently $h_K(\Phi(P))=L\,\mathfrak s_K(P)$ and $h(\Phi(P))=L\,\mathfrak s(P)$ for all $P\in\mathbb P^n_{\mathfrak q}(K)$; in particular $\mathfrak s\ge0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since $q_ir_i=L$, we have $\lVert x_i^{r_i}\rVert_v=(\lVert x_i\rVert_v^{1/q_i})^L$, and $t\mapsto t^L$ is increasing on $[0,\infty)$. Summing over $v$ gives the rest.
head: environment

label: lem:fibres
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fibres}
		Let $n=1$, assume $\gcd(q_0,q_1)=1$, and let $K$ be a field.
		\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
			\item $\Phi\colon\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(K)\to\mathbb P^1(K)$ is surjective.
			\item If $x_0x_1\neq0$ and $\Phi([\mathbf x]_{\mathfrak q})=\Phi([\mathbf y]_{\mathfrak q})$, then $[\mathbf x]_{\mathfrak q}=[\mathbf y]_{\mathfrak q}$.
			\item $\Phi^{-1}([1:0])=\{[a:0]_{\mathfrak q}:a\in K^*\}$, and $[a:0]_{\mathfrak q}=[a':0]_{\mathfrak q}$ if and only if $a'/a\in K^{*q_0}$; similarly for $[0:1]$. If $K$ is a number field, all these points have weighted height $0$.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) The points $[1:0]$, $[0:1]$ are images of $[1:0]_{\mathfrak q}$, $[0:1]_{\mathfrak q}$. For $t\in K^*$ choose $u,v\in\mathbb Z$ with $uq_1-vq_0=1$; then $\Phi([t^u:t^v]_{\mathfrak q})=[t^{uq_1}:t^{vq_0}]=[t:1]$.
		(b) Write $y_i=t_ix_i$; the hypothesis gives $t_0^{q_1}=t_1^{q_0}$. With $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ such that $aq_0+bq_1=1$ and $\lambda=t_0^at_1^b$ we get $\lambda^{q_0}=t_0^{aq_0+bq_1}=t_0$ and $\lambda^{q_1}=t_1^{aq_0+bq_1}=t_1$, so $\mathbf y=\lambda\ast\mathbf x$.
		(c) The first assertions are immediate, and $\mathfrak s_K([a:0]_{\mathfrak q})=q_0^{-1}\sum_v\log\lVert a\rVert_v=0$.
head: environment

label: rem:northcott
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:northcott}
		If $q_0\ge2$, then $\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$ contains the infinitely many points $[a:0]_{\mathfrak q}$, $a\in\mathbb Q^*/\mathbb Q^{*q_0}$, all of height $0$. They define a single point of the variety $\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}$. Northcott's theorem fails for $\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$ but holds for its image under $\Phi$, which is why exceptional sets below have the form $\Phi^{-1}(Z)$ with $Z$ finite.
head: environment

label: lem:integral
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:integral}
		Every $P\in\mathbb P^n_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$ has a $\mathfrak q$-reduced representative. For every representative $\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^{n+1}$ of $P$,
		\[
		\mathfrak s(P)=\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}-\sum_p\mu_p(\mathbf x)\log p,\qquad \mu_p(\mathbf x)=\min_i\frac{v_p(x_i)}{q_i}.
		\]
		If $\mathbf x$ is $\mathfrak q$-reduced and $g=\gcd(x_0,\dots,x_n)$, then
		\[
		\frac{1}{\max_iq_i}\log\operatorname{rad}(g)\ \le\ \log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}-\mathfrak s(P)\ \le\ \log\operatorname{rad}(g),
		\]
		and the right-hand inequality is strict if $g>1$. In particular $\mathfrak s(P)=\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}$ if and only if $g=1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: If $b$ is a common denominator of a rational representative $\mathbf x$, then $b\ast\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^{n+1}$; while some prime satisfies $p^{q_i}\mid x_i$ for all $i$, replace $\mathbf x$ by $p^{-1}\ast\mathbf x$, which lowers $\sum_i|x_i|$. The formula holds because $\log\max_i|x_i|_p^{1/q_i}=-\mu_p(\mathbf x)\log p$. If $\mathbf x$ is $\mathfrak q$-reduced, then $\mu_p(\mathbf x)<1$ for every $p$. Moreover $\mu_p(\mathbf x)=0$ if $p\nmid g$, and $\mu_p(\mathbf x)\ge1/\max_iq_i$ if $p\mid g$.
head: environment

label: ex:height
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:height}
		For $\mathfrak q=(2,3)$ and $\mathbf x=(2,4)$ we get $\mathfrak s(P)=\tfrac16\log2$ and $\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}=\tfrac23\log2$; indeed $\Phi(P)=[1:2]$ and $h(\Phi(P))=\log2=6\,\mathfrak s(P)$. So $H(\Phi(P))\neq|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^L$ in general, even for $\mathfrak q$-reduced $\mathbf x$.
head: environment

label: def:diagonal
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:diagonal}
		For $\mathbf c\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}$ the \emph{diagonal form} of weighted degree $L$ is $F_{\mathbf c}=\sum_ic_ix_i^{r_i}$, and $H_{\mathbf c}=\{F_{\mathbf c}=0\}\subset\mathbb P^n_{\mathfrak q}$ is the corresponding \emph{diagonal hypersurface}.
head: environment

label: lem:weilcompare
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:weilcompare}
		$\zeta_{\mathbf c,v}(P)=\lambda_{\mathbf c,v}(\Phi(P))$ and $\zeta_{\mathbf c,v}(P)\ge-N_v\log(n+1)$. Hence $\zeta_{\mathbf c,\cdot}$ is a Weil function for the Cartier divisor $\Phi^*\Lambda_{\mathbf c}$ on $\mathbb P^n_{\mathfrak q}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The identity follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:veronese} and the bound from
		\[
		\lVert \ell_{\mathbf c}(\mathbf y)\rVert_v\le(n+1)^{N_v}\lVert \mathbf c\rVert_v\max_i\lVert y_i\rVert_v;
		\]
		the last assertion follows from functoriality of Weil functions \cite[Thm.~8.8]{Vojta2011}.
head: environment

label: prop:fmt
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:fmt}
		Let $\mathbf c\in k^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}$, $P\in\mathbb P^n_{\mathfrak q}(k)\setminus H_{\mathbf c}$ and $S\subset M_k$ finite. With $m_S(\mathbf c,P)=\sum_{v\in S}\zeta_{\mathbf c,v}(P)$ and $N_S(\mathbf c,P)=\sum_{v\notin S}\zeta_{\mathbf c,v}(P)$,
		\[
		m_S(\mathbf c,P)+N_S(\mathbf c,P)=L\,\mathfrak s_k(P)+h_k([\mathbf c]).
		\]
head: environment
name: Weighted first main theorem

title: Proof
body_md: Sum over $v\in M_k$ and apply the product formula to $F_{\mathbf c}(\mathbf x)\in k^*$.
head: environment

label: def:chordal
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:chordal}
		Let $n=1$ and $\alpha=[\alpha_0:\alpha_1]_{\mathfrak q}\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ with representative $\mathbf a=(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$. Put
		\[
		F_\alpha(X_0,X_1)=\alpha_1^{r_1}X_0^{r_0}-\alpha_0^{r_0}X_1^{r_1},\qquad \delta_v(P,\alpha)=\frac{\lVert F_\alpha(\mathbf x)\rVert_v}{\lVert \mathbf x\rVert_{v,\mathfrak q}^L\,\lVert \mathbf a\rVert_{v,\mathfrak q}^L}\quad(P=[\mathbf x]_{\mathfrak q}).
		\]
		We call $\delta_v$ the \emph{weighted chordal distance}.
head: environment

label: lem:chordal
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:chordal}
		$\delta_v(P,\alpha)$ is independent of representatives, and $\delta_v(P,\alpha)=\delta_v(\Phi(P),\Phi(\alpha))$. In particular $\delta_v(P,\alpha)=0$ if and only if $\Phi(P)=\Phi(\alpha)$, and $-\log\delta_v(P,\alpha)=\zeta_{\mathbf c,v}(P)$ for $\mathbf c=(\alpha_1^{r_1},-\alpha_0^{r_0})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: With $\mathbf y=(x_0^{r_0},x_1^{r_1})$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\alpha_0^{r_0},\alpha_1^{r_1})$ one has $F_\alpha(\mathbf x)=y_0\beta_1-y_1\beta_0$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:veronese} identifies the denominators; note $\lVert \mathbf c\rVert_v=\lVert \mathbf a\rVert_{v,\mathfrak q}^L$.
head: environment

label: thm:roth
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:roth}
		Let $S\subset M_k$ be finite and $\beta_v\in\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ for $v\in S$. For every $\epsilon>0$ and $c\in\mathbb R$,
		\[
		\sum_{v\in S}-\log\delta_v(y,\beta_v)\le(2+\epsilon)\,h_k(y)+c
		\]
		for all but finitely many $y\in\mathbb P^1(k)$.
head: environment
name: Roth

label: thm:wroth
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Weighted Roth theorem

title: Proof
body_md: By Lemmas~\ref{lem:chordal} and~\ref{lem:veronese} this is Theorem~\ref{thm:roth} for $y=\Phi(P)$ and $\beta_v=\Phi(\alpha_v)$.
head: environment

label: cor:rothQ
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:rothQ}
		Let $\alpha\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ and $\epsilon>0$. There is $C=C(\alpha,\mathfrak q,\epsilon)>0$ such that $|F_\alpha(\mathbf x)|\ge C|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{-(1+\epsilon)L}$ for every $\mathfrak q$-reduced $\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $F_\alpha(\mathbf x)\neq0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Write $P=[\mathbf x]_{\mathfrak q}$, so that $\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)=|F_\alpha(\mathbf x)|/(|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^L|\mathbf a|_{\mathfrak q}^L)$, and let $Z$ be given by Theorem~\ref{thm:wroth} with $k=\mathbb Q$, $S=\{\infty\}$, $c=0$. If $\Phi(P)\notin Z$, then Lemma~\ref{lem:integral} gives $-\log\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)\le(2+\epsilon)L\,\mathfrak s(P)\le(2+\epsilon)L\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}$, whence $|F_\alpha(\mathbf x)|\ge|\mathbf a|_{\mathfrak q}^L|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{-(1+\epsilon)L}$. If $\Phi(P)=z\in Z$ with $z\neq\Phi(\alpha)$, then $\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)=\delta_\infty(z,\Phi(\alpha))=:\delta_z>0$, and $|F_\alpha(\mathbf x)|=\delta_z|\mathbf a|_{\mathfrak q}^L|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^L\ge\delta_z|\mathbf a|_{\mathfrak q}^L|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{-(1+\epsilon)L}$ because $|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}\ge1$.
head: environment

label: prop:optimal
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:optimal}
		Assume $\gcd(q_0,q_1)=1$, and let $\alpha\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ with $\Phi(\alpha)=[b:1]$, $b\in\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q$. There are infinitely many $P\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$, with distinct images under $\Phi$, such that $-\log\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)\ge2L\,\mathfrak s(P)-\log2$.

title: Proof

label: rem:nonintegral
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:nonintegral}
		The points in Proposition~\ref{prop:optimal} are in general not integral. For instance, if $\mathfrak q=(1,2)$ and $u$ is squarefree, the $\mathfrak q$-reduced representative of $\Phi^{-1}([u:v])$ is $(u,uv)$, whose coordinates have greatest common divisor $|u|$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:integral} gives $\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}-\mathfrak s(P)=\tfrac12\log|u|$. This is the source of the gap between Theorem~\ref{thm:wroth} and the behaviour of integral points studied next.
head: environment

label: lem:integralpoints
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Existence is Lemma~\ref{lem:integral}. If $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$ are $\mathfrak q$-reduced and $\mathbf y=\lambda\ast\mathbf x$ with $\lambda=a/c$ in lowest terms, then $c^{q_0}\mid x_0$ and $c^{q_1}\mid x_1$, so $c=1$ by reducedness, and $a=\pm1$ by symmetry. The comparison of heights is Lemma~\ref{lem:integral}.
		(b) The first claim is clear. Injectivity away from $[1:0],[0:1]$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:fibres}(b); each of these two points has at most the two integral preimages $[\pm1:0]_{\mathfrak q}$, respectively $[0:\pm1]_{\mathfrak q}$. Signs can be absorbed because $q_0$ or $q_1$ is odd.
		(c) Up to a factor at most $2$, the first count is the number of coprime pairs with $|x_0|\le T^{q_0}$ and $|x_1|\le T^{q_1}$, which is $\asymp T^{q_0+q_1}$ by M\"obius inversion. The second is the number of $y\in\mathbb P^1(\mathbb Q)$ with $H(y)\le T^L$, which is $\asymp T^{2L}$.
head: environment

label: rem:heuristic
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:heuristic}
		Fix $\alpha$ with $\Phi(\alpha)=[b:1]$, $b\in\mathbb R^*$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:integralpoints}(c), the integral points with $\mathfrak s(P)\approx\log T$ and $\Phi(P)$ near $b$ give about $T^{q_0+q_1}$ fractions of height about $T^L$. If these were randomly distributed, the closest to $b$ would be at distance about $T^{-(q_0+q_1)}$, that is, $-\log\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)\approx(q_0+q_1)\mathfrak s(P)$. The same heuristic for all rational points gives the exponent $2L$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:wroth}. Since $q_0+q_1<2L$ unless $\mathfrak q=(1,1)$, Theorem~\ref{thm:wroth} should be far from optimal on integral points.
head: environment

label: conj:integral
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj:integral}
		Let $\alpha\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ with $\Phi(\alpha)\notin\{[0:1],[1:0]\}$ and $\epsilon>0$. Then
		\[
		-\log\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)\le(q_0+q_1+\epsilon)\,\mathfrak s(P)+O(1)
		\]
		for all $P\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Z)$ with $\Phi(P)\neq\Phi(\alpha)$. Equivalently, $|F_\alpha(\mathbf x)|\ge C\,|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{L-q_0-q_1-\epsilon}$ for all coprime $\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $F_\alpha(\mathbf x)\neq0$.

label: conj:radical
title: Conjecture
head: environment
name: Radical form

label: lem:deduction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:deduction}
		Let $G\in\mathbb Z[U,V]$ be squarefree of degree $d$ with $G(0,1)G(1,0)\neq0$, let $S\subset M_{\mathbb Q}$ be finite with $\infty\in S$, and for $v\in S$ let $A_v\subset\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ be a finite set on which $\Phi$ is injective, with $\Phi(A_v)\subset Z(G)$. There is $C>0$ such that
		\[
		\prod_{v\in S}\prod_{\alpha\in A_v}\delta_v(P,\alpha)\ \ge\ C\,\operatorname{rad}\bigl(G(u,v)\bigr)\,H(\Phi(P))^{-d}
		\]
		for all $P\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$ with $\Phi(P)=[u:v]$, $u,v$ coprime integers and $G(u,v)\neq0$. Consequently, if Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} holds for $\mathfrak q$ and $G$, then for every $\epsilon>0$
		\[
		\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{\alpha\in A_v}-\log\delta_v(P,\alpha)\le(q_0+q_1+\epsilon)\,\mathfrak s(P)+O(1)
		\]
		for all $P\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Z)$ with $\Phi(P)\notin Z(G)$. In particular Conjecture~\ref{conj:integral} holds for every $\alpha$ with $\Phi(\alpha)\in Z(G)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $y=\Phi(P)$ and $S_f=S\setminus\{\infty\}$. For a nonzero integer $m$ one has $\operatorname{rad}(m)\le\prod_{p\in S_f}p\cdot\prod_{v\in S}|m|_v$. Factor $G=g_0\prod_{\beta\in Z(G)}(\beta_1U-\beta_0V)$ over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$. Since $\max\{|u|_p,|v|_p\}=1$ for finite $p$ and $\max\{|u|,|v|\}=H(y)$, we get
		\[
		\prod_{v\in S}|G(u,v)|_v=C_G\,H(y)^{d}\prod_{v\in S}\prod_{\beta\in Z(G)}\delta_v(y,\beta),
		\]
		where $C_G>0$ does not depend on $y$. Every factor $\delta_v(y,\beta)$ is at most $2$, and for each $v$ the points $\Phi(\alpha)$, $\alpha\in A_v$, are distinct elements of $Z(G)$. Hence $\prod_{v}\prod_{\alpha\in A_v}\delta_v(y,\Phi(\alpha))$ is at least a positive constant times $\prod_v\prod_{\beta}\delta_v(y,\beta)$, and the first inequality follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:chordal}. For the second, let $P$ be integral with coprime representative $\mathbf x$. The finitely many $P$ with $x_0x_1=0$ only affect the constant. Otherwise $H(y)=|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^L$ and $\mathfrak s(P)=\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}$, so Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} and the first inequality give $\prod_{v\in S}\prod_{\alpha\in A_v}\delta_v(P,\alpha)\ge C'|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{-(q_0+q_1)-\epsilon}$.

label: lem:radical
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $D\subset\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ be the zero set of $\Psi$. By the prescribed-set form of Belyi's theorem \cite[Thm.~31.1]{Vojta2011}, applied to the Galois-stable zero divisor $D$ of $\Psi$, there is a finite morphism $f\colon\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}$ of some degree $N$, ramified only over $\{0,1,\infty\}$, with $D\subset E:=f^{-1}(\{0,1,\infty\})$. Write $f=[A:C]$ with coprime forms $A,C\in\mathbb Z[U,V]$ of degree $N$, and put $B=C-A$. By Riemann--Hurwitz, $E$ has exactly $N+2$ points. Let $R\in\mathbb Z[U,V]$ be the product of the distinct primitive irreducible factors of $ABC$, so that $\deg R=N+2$. Since $\Psi$ is squarefree with zeros in $E$, we can write $R=\Psi_0\Psi'$, where $\Psi_0$ is the primitive part of $\Psi$ and $\deg\Psi'=N+2-n$.
		
		The finitely many $y\in E(\mathbb Q)\setminus D$ have finitely many coprime representatives, and they can be absorbed into $c$. So let $(u,v)$ be coprime with $y=[u:v]\notin E$, and write $M=\max\{|u|,|v|\}$. There is a nonzero integer $\rho$, depending on the resultant of $A$ and $C$, such that $g:=\gcd(A(u,v),C(u,v))$ divides $\rho$. Moreover $\max\{|A(u,v)|,|C(u,v)|\}\ge c_0M^N$, because $A$ and $C$ have no common zero. Applying $abc$ to the coprime triple $A(u,v)/g+B(u,v)/g=C(u,v)/g$ gives
		\[
		c_0M^N\le|\rho|\,K_\epsilon\,\operatorname{rad}\bigl(A(u,v)B(u,v)C(u,v)\bigr)^{1+\epsilon}.
		\]
		Every prime dividing $ABC(u,v)$ divides the content of $ABC$ or $R(u,v)$, and
		\[
		\operatorname{rad}(R(u,v))\le\operatorname{rad}(\Psi(u,v))\,|\Psi'(u,v)|\le c_1\operatorname{rad}(\Psi(u,v))\,M^{N+2-n}.
		\]
		Hence $M^{N}\ll\bigl(\operatorname{rad}(\Psi(u,v))\,M^{N+2-n}\bigr)^{1+\epsilon}$, which gives $\operatorname{rad}(\Psi(u,v))\gg M^{n-2-\epsilon N}$. Replacing $\epsilon$ by $\epsilon/N$ proves the lemma.

label: thm:abcgeneral
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:abcgeneral}
		Assume the $abc$ conjecture.
		\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
			\item Let $G\in\mathbb Z[U,V]$ be squarefree of degree $d$ with $G(0,1)G(1,0)\neq0$, and let $\epsilon>0$. There is $c>0$ such that
			\[
			\operatorname{rad}\bigl(G(u,v)\bigr)\ge c\,H(\Phi(P))^{d-\epsilon}\,\mathcal S_{\mathbb Z}(P)^{-(q_0+q_1)}
			\]
			for all $P\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$ with $\Phi(P)=[u:v]$, $u,v$ coprime and $uv\,G(u,v)\neq0$. In particular Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} holds for all $\mathfrak q$ and $G$.
			\item Let $S\subset M_{\mathbb Q}$ be finite, and for $v\in S$ let $A_v\subset\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ be a finite set on which $\Phi$ is injective, with $\Phi(A_v)\cap\{[0:1],[1:0]\}=\emptyset$. Put $B=\bigcup_v\Phi(A_v)$. For every $\epsilon>0$ there is $c'\in\mathbb R$ such that
			\[
			\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{\alpha\in A_v}-\log\delta_v(P,\alpha)\le(q_0+q_1+\epsilon)\log\mathcal S_{\mathbb Z}(P)+c'
			\]
			for all $P\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$ with $\Phi(P)\notin B$. For $P\in\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Z)$ the right-hand side equals $(q_0+q_1+\epsilon)\mathfrak s(P)+c'$; in particular Conjecture~\ref{conj:integral} holds.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Let $G_0$ be the primitive part of $G$. Since $U$ and $V$ do not divide $G$, the form $\Psi=UV\,G_0$ is squarefree of degree $d+2$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:radical} gives $\operatorname{rad}(\Psi(u,v))\ge c\,H(\Phi(P))^{d-\epsilon}$. Let $\mathbf x$ be a $\mathfrak q$-reduced representative of $P$. Then $u\mid x_0^{q_1}$ and $v\mid x_1^{q_0}$, so $\operatorname{rad}(u)\operatorname{rad}(v)\le|x_0x_1|\le\mathcal S_{\mathbb Z}(P)^{q_0+q_1}$, and therefore $\operatorname{rad}(\Psi(u,v))\le\mathcal S_{\mathbb Z}(P)^{q_0+q_1}\operatorname{rad}(G(u,v))$. For integral $P$ one has $H(\Phi(P))=|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^L$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathbb Z}(P)=|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}$, which gives Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} after replacing $\epsilon$ by $\epsilon/L$.
		
		(b) Adding the archimedean place with $A_\infty=\emptyset$ changes nothing, so we may assume $\infty\in S$. Let $G$ be the product of the primitive irreducible forms whose zero sets are the Galois orbits of the points of $B$; it is squarefree, and $G(0,1)G(1,0)\neq0$. If $\Phi(P)\in\{[0:1],[1:0]\}$, each $\delta_v(P,\alpha)=\delta_v(\Phi(P),\Phi(\alpha))$ is a fixed positive number, and since $\mathcal S_{\mathbb Z}(P)\ge1$ such $P$ only affect the constant. Otherwise $G(u,v)\neq0$, because a rational zero of $G$ would lie in $B$. Lemma~\ref{lem:deduction} and part (a) give
		\[
		\prod_{v}\prod_{\alpha\in A_v}\delta_v(P,\alpha)\ge C\,H(\Phi(P))^{-\epsilon}\,\mathcal S_{\mathbb Z}(P)^{-(q_0+q_1)}.
		\]
		Since $H(\Phi(P))=\exp(L\,\mathfrak s(P))\le\mathcal S_{\mathbb Z}(P)^L$, replacing $\epsilon$ by $\epsilon/L$ proves the inequality. The last assertion follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:integralpoints}(a).

label: prop:abcwabc
title: Proposition

\label{prop:abcwabc}
		The $abc$ conjecture implies $\mathrm{wABC}(p,q;A,B)$ for all $p,q,A,B$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $x,y$ be coprime with $xy
eq0$ and $c=Ax^p+By^q
eq0$, and let $g=\gcd(Ax^p,By^q)$. A prime $\ell\mid g$ divides $AB$, since otherwise it would divide $x$ and $y$. If $\ell
mid x$ then $v_\ell(g)\le v_\ell(A)$, and if $\ell
mid y$ then $v_\ell(g)\le v_\ell(B)$; hence $g\mid AB$. Applying $abc$ to $Ax^p/g+By^q/g=c/g$ gives
		\[
		\max\{|x|^p,|y|^q\}\le\max\{|Ax^p|,|By^q|\}\le|AB|\,K_\epsilon igl(\operatorname{rad}(AB)\,|xy|\,\operatorname{rad}(c) igr)^{1+\epsilon}.\qedhere
		\]

label: prop:kummer
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:kummer}
		Let $b\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^*$ and $n\ge1$ with $b^n=r_0/r_1$, where $r_0,r_1$ are nonzero coprime integers, and put $G_n=r_1U^n-r_0V^n$. If $\mathrm{wABC}(nq_1,nq_0;r_1,-r_0)$ holds, then Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} holds for $\mathfrak q$ and $G_n$. Consequently, the $S$-adic inequality of Lemma~\ref{lem:deduction} and Conjecture~\ref{conj:integral} hold for every $\alpha$ with $\Phi(\alpha)=[\zeta b:1]$, $\zeta^n=1$. For $n=1$ this covers all rational targets other than $[0:1]$ and $[1:0]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The form $G_n$ has the $n$ distinct zeros $[\zeta b:1]$, so it is squarefree, and $G_n(0,1)G_n(1,0)=-r_0r_1\neq0$. For coprime $\mathbf x$ with $x_0x_1G_n(x_0^{q_1},x_1^{q_0})\neq0$, the hypothesis applied to $(x,y)=(x_0,x_1)$ gives
		\[
		|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{nL}=\max\{|x_0|^{nq_1},|x_1|^{nq_0}\}\le K\bigl(|x_0x_1|\,\operatorname{rad}(G_n(x_0^{q_1},x_1^{q_0}))\bigr)^{1+\epsilon}.
		\]
		Since $|x_0x_1|\le|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{q_0+q_1}$, this yields $\operatorname{rad}(G_n(x_0^{q_1},x_1^{q_0}))\gg|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{nL-q_0-q_1-\epsilon nL}$, which is Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} for $G_n$ after renaming $\epsilon$. The rest follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:deduction}.

label: def:wbelyi
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:wbelyi}
		Let $m_0,m_1\ge2$ be integers and $S\subset\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ a finite set. A \emph{weighted Belyi map of signature $(m_0,m_1)$ for $S$} is a finite morphism $f\colon\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}$, unramified outside $\{0,1,\infty\}$, such that every point of $f^{-1}(0)$ has ramification index $m_0$, every point of $f^{-1}(1)$ has ramification index $m_1$, and $S\subset f^{-1}(\infty)$.

label: thm:wbelyiexists
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:wbelyiexists}
		Let
		\[
		J(\lambda)=\frac{4(\lambda^2-\lambda+1)^3}{27\lambda^2(\lambda-1)^2}.
		\]
		If $g\colon\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}$ is unramified outside $\{0,1,\infty\}$ and $S\subset g^{-1}(\{0,1,\infty\})$, then $J\circ g$ is a weighted Belyi map of signature $(3,2)$ for $S$. In particular such maps exist for every finite $S\subset\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$.

title: Proof

label: thm:wbelyi
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:wbelyi}
		Let $G\in\mathbb Z[U,V]$ be squarefree of degree $d\ge1$ with $G(0,1)G(1,0)\neq0$. There is a finite set $E_G$ of positive integers, depending only on $G$, with the following property. If $\mathrm{wABC}(3,2;4e,-1)$ holds for every $e\in E_G$, then Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} holds for $G$ and every coprime weight vector $\mathfrak q$, and hence so do the conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:deduction}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $S=\{[0:1],[1:0]\}\cup Z(G)$ and let $g$ be a Belyi map for $S$ of degree $n$, written $g=[G_1:G_2]$ with coprime $G_1,G_2\in\mathbb Z[U,V]$ of degree $n$. Let $\rho$ be a nonzero integer such that $\gcd(G_1(u,v),G_2(u,v))$ divides $\rho$ for all coprime $(u,v)$ (for instance the resultant of $G_1$ and $G_2$), and let $E_G$ be the set of positive divisors of $27\rho^3$. Homogenizing the identity $4\varphi^3-\psi^2=27\omega$ gives
		\[
		4X^3-Y^2=27W,
		\]
		where
		\[
		\begin{aligned}
			X&=G_1^2-G_1G_2+G_2^2,\\
			Y&=(G_1+G_2)(G_1-2G_2)(2G_1-G_2),\\
			W&=G_1^2G_2^2(G_1-G_2)^2
		\end{aligned}
		\]
		are forms of degrees $2n$, $3n$ and $6n$. In the notation of Theorem~\ref{thm:wbelyiexists}, $J\circ g=[4X^3:27W]$ and $J\circ g-1=Y^2/(27W)$.
		
		Let $\mathbf x$ be coprime with $x_0x_1G(u,v)\neq0$, where $(u,v)=(x_0^{q_1},x_1^{q_0})$, and put $y=[u:v]$ and $H=H(y)=|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^L$. The rational points $y$ with $g(y)\in\{0,1,\infty,-1,\tfrac12,2\}$ are finite in number, and each comes from at most four coprime pairs $\mathbf x$. At these $\operatorname{rad}(G(u,v))\ge1$, so they only affect the constant. For the remaining $\mathbf x$, the integers $\tilde x=X(u,v)$, $\tilde y=Y(u,v)$ and $\tilde w=W(u,v)$ are nonzero.
		
		\emph{Step 1: the common factor.} Write $G_1(u,v)=hs'$ and $G_2(u,v)=ht'$ with $h\mid\rho$ and $\gcd(s',t')=1$. Then $\tilde x=h^2X_0$ and $\tilde y=h^3Y_0$ with $X_0=s'^2-s't'+t'^2$ and $Y_0=(s'+t')(s'-2t')(2s'-t')$. The resultant of these two binary forms is $\pm27$, so $\gcd(X_0,Y_0)\mid27$. Hence $e:=\gcd(\tilde x,\tilde y)$ divides $27h^3$, and $e\in E_G$.
		
		\emph{Step 2: the triple.} Write $\tilde x=ex'$ and $\tilde y=ey'$, with $x',y'$ coprime and nonzero. Then
		\[
		4e\,x'^3-y'^2=27\tilde w/e^2=:c'\neq0,
		\]
		and $c'$ divides $27\tilde w$.
		
		\emph{Step 3: size.} The forms $X^3$ and $W$ of degree $6n$ have no common zero on $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$: a common zero $z$ would satisfy both $\varphi(g(z))=0$ and $g(z)\in\{0,1,\infty\}$. Hence $\max\{|\tilde x|^3,|\tilde w|\}\gg H^{6n}$. Since $27|\tilde w|\le5\max\{|\tilde x|^3,|\tilde y|^2\}$, we get $\max\{|x'|^3,|y'|^2\}\gg H^{6n}$. On the other hand $|x'|\le|\tilde x|\ll H^{2n}$ and $|y'|\le|\tilde y|\ll H^{3n}$.
		
		\emph{Step 4: the radical.} The zero set of $G_1G_2(G_1-G_2)$ is $g^{-1}(\{0,1,\infty\})$, which has $n+2$ points by Riemann--Hurwitz and contains $S$. Let $T$ be the product of the distinct primitive irreducible factors of $G_1G_2(G_1-G_2)$. Then $\deg T=n+2$ and $T=\pm UV\,G_0\,T'$, where $G_0$ is the primitive part of $G$ and $\deg T'=n-d$. Every prime dividing $\tilde w$ divides the content of $G_1G_2(G_1-G_2)$ or $T(u,v)$. Therefore
		\[
		\begin{aligned}
			\operatorname{rad}(c')
			&\le3\operatorname{rad}(\tilde w)
			\ll\operatorname{rad}(u)\operatorname{rad}(v)\operatorname{rad}(G(u,v))\,|T'(u,v)|\\
			&\ll|x_0x_1|\,\operatorname{rad}(G(u,v))\,H^{n-d}.
		\end{aligned}
		\]
		
		\emph{Step 5: conclusion.} Applying $\mathrm{wABC}(3,2;4e,-1)$ to $(x',y')$ and using Steps 3 and 4, we obtain
		\[
		H^{6n}\ll\bigl(H^{2n}H^{3n}\,|x_0x_1|\,\operatorname{rad}(G(u,v))\,H^{n-d}\bigr)^{1+\epsilon}.
		\]
		Using $|x_0x_1|\le|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{q_0+q_1}$ and $H=|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^L$, this gives
		\[
		\operatorname{rad}(G(u,v))\gg H^{d-6n\epsilon}|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{-(q_0+q_1)}=|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{dL-q_0-q_1-6nL\epsilon}.
		\]
		Replacing $\epsilon$ by $\epsilon/(6nL)$ completes the proof. Note that $E_G$ depends only on $g$, and hence only on $G$, and not on $\mathfrak q$.

label: prop:equiv
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:equiv}
		The $abc$ conjecture holds if and only if\linebreak $\mathrm{wABC}(3,2;4e,-1)$ holds for each
		\[
		e\in\{1,3,9,27\}.
		\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
One direction is Proposition~\ref{prop:abcwabc}. Conversely, let $a+b=c$ with $a,b,c$ coprime and $abc\neq0$, and put $M=\max\{|a|,|b|,|c|\}$. With $X,Y,W$ as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:wbelyi}, taking $G_1=U$ and $G_2=V$ and evaluating at $(a,c)$, we get
		\[
		\tilde x=a^2-ac+c^2,\qquad \tilde y=(a+c)(a-2c)(2a-c),\qquad 4\tilde x^3-\tilde y^2=27a^2b^2c^2.
		\]
		If $\tilde y=0$, then $a=-c$, $a=2c$ or $c=2a$, and coprimality forces $M\le2$. Otherwise, since $\gcd(a,c)=1$, the integer $e=\gcd(\tilde x,\tilde y)$ divides $27$. Write $\tilde x=ex'$ and $\tilde y=ey'$. Then $2\tilde x=a^2+c^2+(a-c)^2\ge\max\{a^2,c^2\}$, and $M\le2\max\{|a|,|c|\}$, so $\tilde x\ge M^2/8$. Also $|\tilde y|\le18M^3$ and $\operatorname{rad}(4ex'^3-y'^2)\le3\operatorname{rad}(abc)$. Now $\mathrm{wABC}(3,2;4e,-1)$ gives
		\[
		M^6\ll\bigl(M^5\operatorname{rad}(abc)\bigr)^{1+\epsilon},
		\]
		Thus
		\[
		\operatorname{rad}(abc)\gg M^{6/(1+\epsilon)-5}=M^{(1-5\epsilon)/(1+\epsilon)}.
		\]
		Given $\eta>0$, choose $\epsilon>0$ so small that $(1-5\epsilon)/(1+\epsilon)\ge1-\eta$. Then $M\ll_\eta\operatorname{rad}(abc)^{1/(1-\eta)}$, which is the usual $abc$ inequality after the standard reparametrization of the exponent.

label: cor:universal
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:universal}
		Let $\mathfrak q=(2,3)$. If Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} holds for $\mathfrak q$ and each of the four linear forms $4eU-V$, $e\in\{1,3,9,27\}$, then the $abc$ conjecture holds. Consequently Conjectures~\ref{conj:integral} and~\ref{conj:radical} hold for all coprime weight vectors, all forms $G$ and all algebraic targets.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For $\mathfrak q=(2,3)$ we have $L=6$ and $q_0+q_1=5$. For $G=4eU-V$, Conjecture~\ref{conj:radical} states that $\operatorname{rad}(4e\,x_0^3-x_1^2)\gg|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{1-\epsilon}$ for coprime $\mathbf x$ with $x_0x_1(4ex_0^3-x_1^2)\neq0$. Apply this to $(x_0,x_1)=(x',y')$ from the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:equiv}. There $|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}\ge|x'|^{1/2}\ge(\tilde x/27)^{1/2}\gg M$ and $\operatorname{rad}(4ex'^3-y'^2)\le3\operatorname{rad}(abc)$, so $\operatorname{rad}(abc)\gg M^{1-\epsilon}$. The last assertion follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:abcgeneral} and Lemma~\ref{lem:deduction}.
head: environment

label: rem:wbelyi
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:wbelyi}
		\begin{enumerate}[(a),leftmargin=*]
			\item Theorem~\ref{thm:wbelyi} and Proposition~\ref{prop:equiv} show that weighted Belyi maps allow Theorem~\ref{thm:abcgeneral}(a) to be derived from the weighted $abc$ conjecture of signature $(3,2)$ alone, but this does not weaken the hypothesis, since that conjecture is equivalent to $abc$. Corollary~\ref{cor:universal} shows that the radical form of the conjecture for $\mathfrak q=(2,3)$ and four rational targets already implies all other cases.
			\item The radical is essential in this argument. For the pairs $(x',y')$ used above, $|4ex'^3-y'^2|=27a^2b^2c^2/e^2\gg M^4$ while $|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}\ll M$. So the form of Conjecture~\ref{conj:integral} with $|F_\alpha(\mathbf x)|$ in place of the radical is automatically satisfied there and gives no information.
			\item Suppose that for some signature $(m_0,m_1)$ there is a weighted Belyi map $f$ of signature $(m_0,m_1)$ for $\{0,1,\infty\}$. The argument of Proposition~\ref{prop:equiv} then shows that $\mathrm{wABC}(m_0,m_1;\cdot,\cdot)$, for finitely many coefficient pairs, implies $abc$. The exponent count uses Riemann--Hurwitz in the form $N/m_0+N/m_1+\#f^{-1}(\infty)=N+2$, where $N=\deg f$. We have not investigated which signatures admit such maps.
			\item In Proposition~\ref{prop:kummer} the power map $t\mapsto t^n$ plays the role of the Belyi map. It respects the stacky structure, which is why a single weighted $abc$ statement suffices there.
		\end{enumerate}

label: prop:danilov
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:danilov}
		Let $\mathfrak q=(2,3)$, so $L=6$ and $q_0+q_1=5$. There are infinitely many coprime $\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $0<|x_0^3-x_1^2|<|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}$. Hence for $\Phi(\alpha)=[1:1]$ the constant $q_0+q_1$ in Conjecture~\ref{conj:integral} and Theorem~\ref{thm:abcgeneral} cannot be lowered.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $t\in\mathbb Z$ put $x_0=5^5t^2-3000t+719$ and $w(t)=5^3t^2-114t+26$. One checks the identity
		\[
		x_0^3-w(t)\bigl(5^6t^2-5^3\cdot123\,t+3781\bigr)^2=27(2t-1)
		\]
		due to Danilov and Elkies \cite{Danilov1982,Elkies2000}. Since $125\,w(t)=(125t-57)^2+1$, the values of $t$ with $w(t)=s^2$ a square correspond to solutions of $X^2-125s^2=-1$ with $X\equiv-57\pmod{125}$. One solution is $(X,s)=(-682,61)$, coming from $t=-5$. Multiplying $-682+61\sqrt{125}$ by powers of a unit $a+b\sqrt{125}$ of norm $1$ with $a\equiv1$ and $b\equiv0\pmod{125}$ preserves the congruence, so there are infinitely many such $t$. For these put $x_1=s(5^6t^2-5^3\cdot123\,t+3781)$. Then $x_0^3-x_1^2=27(2t-1)\neq0$. Since $4x_0\equiv1\pmod{2t-1}$ and $x_0\equiv-(t^2+1)\not\equiv0\pmod3$, we have $\gcd(x_0,27(2t-1))=1$, and hence $\gcd(x_0,x_1)=1$. The quadratic $5^5t^2-3000t+719$ is negative only for $t$ in an interval inside $(0.46,0.5)$, which contains no integer; hence $x_0>0$ and $|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}\ge x_0^{1/2}$. Along the Pell sequence one has $|t|\to\infty$, hence $x_0\to\infty$ and $\mathfrak s([x_0:x_1]_{\mathfrak q})\to\infty$. Finally $27|2t-1|/x_0^{1/2}\to54/5^{5/2}<1$ as $|t|\to\infty$. For $\alpha=[1:1]_{\mathfrak q}$ this gives $-\log\delta_\infty(P,\alpha)=-\log|x_0^3-x_1^2|+6\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}\ge5\,\mathfrak s(P)$.

label: prop:functionfield
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:functionfield}
		Let $x_0,x_1\in\mathbf k[t]$ be coprime and not both constant, and let $b\in\mathbf k^*$. If $F=x_0^{q_1}-b\,x_1^{q_0}\neq0$, then
		\[
		\deg F\ge(L-q_0-q_1)\,d_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbf x)+1.
		\]
		For $\mathfrak q=(2,3)$ and $b=1$ the bound is attained, for example by $(x_0,x_1)=(t^2+2,\,t^3+3t)$, and more generally by the pairs of Stothers and Zannier \cite{Stothers1981,Zannier1995}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The polynomials $A=x_0^{q_1}$, $B=-b\,x_1^{q_0}$ and $F=A+B$ are pairwise coprime and not all constant. By Mason--Stothers, $\max\{\deg A,\deg B,\deg F\}\le n_0(ABF)-1$, where $n_0$ counts distinct roots. The left side is at least $\max\{q_1\deg x_0,q_0\deg x_1\}=L\,d_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbf x)$. The right side is at most $\deg x_0+\deg x_1+\deg F-1\le(q_0+q_1)d_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbf x)+\deg F-1$. For the example, $(t^2+2)^3-(t^3+3t)^2=3t^2+8$ has degree $2=(6-5)\cdot1+1$. Zannier shows that for every $\delta\ge1$ there are $f,g$ with $\deg f=2\delta$, $\deg g=3\delta$ and $\deg(f^3-g^2)=\delta+1$. Such pairs are coprime: if $h=\gcd(f,g)\neq1$, apply Mason--Stothers to $f^3/e$, $-g^2/e$ and $(f^3-g^2)/e$ with $e=\gcd(f^3,g^2)$. Using $n_0(fg)\le\deg f+\deg g-1$, this gives $\deg(f^3-g^2)\ge\delta+2$.

label: prop:metric
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: It suffices to treat $b$ in a compact interval $I\subset\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and a fixed $\epsilon$. For coprime $\mathbf x$ let $E_{\mathbf x}=\{b\in I:|x_0^{q_1}-b\,x_1^{q_0}|<|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{L-q_0-q_1-\epsilon}\}$, and let $T\le|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}<2T$ with $T$ large. If $E_{\mathbf x}\neq\emptyset$, then $|x_1|^{q_0}\gg T^L$. Indeed $\max\{|x_0|^{q_1},|x_1|^{q_0}\}=|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^L$, and $|x_0^{q_1}-bx_1^{q_0}|$ is $o(T^L)$ while $b$ is bounded away from $0$ and $\infty$. Hence $E_{\mathbf x}$ is an interval of length $\ll T^{-q_0-q_1-\epsilon}$. There are $\ll T^{q_0+q_1}$ vectors with $|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}<2T$, so $\sum_{T\le|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}<2T}|E_{\mathbf x}|\ll T^{-\epsilon}$, which is summable over $T=2^k$. By the Borel--Cantelli lemma, for this fixed $\epsilon$ almost every $b\in I$ lies in only finitely many $E_{\mathbf x}$. Intersecting the resulting full-measure sets for $\epsilon=1/n$, $n\ge1$, gives one full-measure set on which the asserted conclusion holds for every $\epsilon>0$. The vectors with $x_1=0$ form a finite coprime exceptional set and may be absorbed into the constant. For irrational $b$ the finitely many remaining exceptional $\mathbf x$ have $x_0^{q_1}-bx_1^{q_0}\neq0$, so they can be absorbed into $C$.

label: rem:barrier
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:barrier}
		An unconditional proof of Conjecture~\ref{conj:integral} over $\mathbb Q$ would in particular establish the coprime case of Hall's conjecture. The best unconditional results in that direction come from Baker's method and are of logarithmic strength \cite{Baker1968}. There is also a structural reason why the methods behind Theorem~\ref{thm:wroth} cannot reach the conjecture. The map $\Phi$ identifies $\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\mathbb P^1$ and maps $\mathbb P^1_{\mathfrak q}(\mathbb Q)$ onto $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb Q)$, and on rational points the exponent $2L$ is sharp (Proposition~\ref{prop:optimal}). Any proof of Conjecture~\ref{conj:integral} must therefore use integrality, and in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:abcgeneral} integrality enters only through radicals. We do not know how to use information of this kind in the auxiliary polynomial method or in the subspace theorem.

label: thm:schmidt
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:schmidt}
		Let $S\subset M_k$ be finite and contain the archimedean places, and let $\mathbf c_1,\dots,\mathbf c_t\in\overline{\mathbb Q}^{n+1}$ be in general position. For every $\epsilon>0$ and $c\in\mathbb R$,
		\[
		\sum_{j=1}^t\sum_{v\in S}\lambda_{\mathbf c_j,v}(y)\le(n+1+\epsilon)\,h_k(y)+c
		\]
		for all $y\in\mathbb P^n(k)$ outside a finite union of proper linear subspaces of $\mathbb P^n_k$.
head: environment
name: Schmidt

label: thm:wsubspace
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:wsubspace}
		With $S$, $\mathbf c_1,\dots,\mathbf c_t$, $\epsilon$, $c$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:schmidt}, there are proper linear subspaces $W_1,\dots,W_u\subset\mathbb P^n_k$ such that
		\[
		\sum_{j=1}^t\sum_{v\in S}\zeta_{\mathbf c_j,v}(P)\le(n+1+\epsilon)\,L\,\mathfrak s_k(P)+c
		\]
		for every $P\in\mathbb P^n_{\mathfrak q}(k)\setminus\bigcup_jH_{\mathbf c_j}$ with $\Phi(P)\notin W_1\cup\dots\cup W_u$. The exceptional points lie on finitely many diagonal hypersurfaces $H_{\mathbf c}$, $\mathbf c\in k^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}$.
head: environment
name: Pullback of the subspace theorem

title: Proof
body_md: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:schmidt} to $y=\Phi(P)$, using Lemmas~\ref{lem:weilcompare} and~\ref{lem:veronese}; every proper linear subspace lies in some $\Lambda_{\mathbf c}$, and $\Phi^{-1}(\Lambda_{\mathbf c})=H_{\mathbf c}$.

label: cor:product
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take $k=\mathbb Q$, $S=\{\infty\}$, $c=0$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:wsubspace}. Since
		\[
		\zeta_{\mathbf c_j,\infty}([\mathbf x]_{\mathfrak q})=-\log|F_{\mathbf c_j}(\mathbf x)|+L\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}+\log\lVert \mathbf c_j\rVert_\infty
		\]
		and $\mathfrak s([\mathbf x]_{\mathfrak q})\le\log|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:integral}), the claim holds with $C=\prod_j\lVert \mathbf c_j\rVert_\infty$.
head: environment

label: rem:subspace
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:subspace}
		For $t=n+1$ Corollary~\ref{cor:product} reads $\prod_j|F_{\mathbf c_j}(\mathbf x)|\ge C|\mathbf x|_{\mathfrak q}^{-\epsilon L}$. As in the classical case it has content only when some $\mathbf c_j$ has irrational coordinates; for rational $\mathbf c_j$, Theorem~\ref{thm:wsubspace} is substantial once $S$ contains finite places. The version of Schmidt's theorem with hyperplanes depending on $v$ \cite[Thm.~7.12]{Vojta2011} transfers in the same way. For general weighted hypersurfaces one must embed $\mathbb P^n_{\mathfrak q}$ by a multiple of $\mathcal O(L)$ and use the methods of Corvaja--Zannier~\cite{CZ2004} and Evertse--Ferretti~\cite{EF2008}; see \cite[\S\S20--21]{Vojta2011}.

label: lem:structure
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:structure}
		Every nonzero weighted homogeneous $F$ of weighted degree $D$ can be written uniquely as
		\[
		F(X,Y)=X^aY^b\,G(X^{q_1},Y^{q_0})
		\]
		with $0\le a<q_1$, $0\le b<q_0$ and $G\in\overline{\mathbb Q}[U,V]$ a binary form of degree $\kappa\ge0$; moreover $D=aq_0+bq_1+\kappa L$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: If $q_0i+q_1j=D$ then $i\equiv Dq_0^{-1}\pmod{q_1}$ and $j\equiv Dq_1^{-1}\pmod{q_0}$, so $a,b$ depend only on $D$. Writing $i=a+q_1s$ and $j=b+q_0s'$, we get $s+s'=(D-aq_0-bq_1)/L=:\kappa$ for every monomial.

label: lem:thueroth
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:thueroth}
		Let $G\in\overline{\mathbb Q}[U,V]$ be a binary form of degree $\kappa\ge0$ without repeated factors, and let $\epsilon>0$. There is $C>0$ with $|G(u,v)|\ge C\max\{|u|,|v|\}^{\kappa-2-\epsilon}$ for all coprime $(u,v)\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $G(u,v)\neq0$.
head: environment
name: Thue--Siegel--Roth

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\kappa\ge1$ and $G=g\prod_{i=1}^\kappa(\theta_{i1}U-\theta_{i0}V)$ with distinct $\theta_i\in\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$. For coprime $(u,v)$ and $y=[u:v]$ we have $h(y)=\log\max\{|u|,|v|\}$ and
		\[
		-\log|G(u,v)|=\sum_{i=1}^\kappa\lambda_{\theta_i,\infty}(y)-\kappa\,h(y)+c_G.
		\]
		For $i\neq j$ the function $y\mapsto\max\{\delta_\infty(y,\theta_i),\delta_\infty(y,\theta_j)\}$ is continuous and positive on the compact space $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$. Hence there is $\eta>0$ such that at most one $i$ has $\delta_\infty(y,\theta_i)<\eta$, and so $\sum_i\lambda_{\theta_i,\infty}(y)\le\max_i\lambda_{\theta_i,\infty}(y)+(\kappa-1)\log\eta^{-1}$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:roth}, applied to each $\theta_i$, $\max_i\lambda_{\theta_i,\infty}(y)\le(2+\epsilon)h(y)$ outside a finite set of $y$. Each exceptional $y$ has only the representatives $\pm(u,v)$, and there $G(u,v)\neq0$, so the constant can be adjusted.

label: lem:twopoints
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:twopoints}
		Let $P\in K[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ be nonzero of degree at most $1$ in each variable, and let $\mathbf a,\mathbf b\in K^m$ with $a_\ell\neq b_\ell$ for all $\ell$. Then $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a}(P)+\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b}(P)\le m$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Induction on $m$, the case $m=0$ being trivial. Write $P=(x_1-a_1)A+B=(x_1-b_1)A+B'$ with $A,B\in K[x_2,\dots,x_m]$ and $B'=B+(b_1-a_1)A$, and let $\mathbf a',\mathbf b'$ be $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$ without their first coordinates. Then $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a}P=\min\{1+\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a'}A,\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a'}B\}$ and $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b}P=\min\{1+\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b'}A,\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b'}B'\}$. If $A=0$ we conclude by induction. Otherwise put $s=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a'}A$ and $s'=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b'}A$, so $s+s'\le m-1$. The claim is clear unless $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a}P=s+1$, $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b}P=s'+1$ and $s+s'=m-1$. In that case $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a'}B>s$ and $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b'}B'>s'$. The latter and $B=B'-(b_1-a_1)A$ give $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b'}B=s'$, so $B\neq0$, and induction yields $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a'}B\le m-1-s'=s$, a contradiction.

There is no nonzero $P\in\mathbb Z[x_1,\dots,x_9]$ with $\deg_{x_\ell}P\le\lfloor d_\ell/q_\ell\rfloor$ for all $\ell$ and $t_{\mathfrak q}(P;(\alpha,\dots,\alpha);\mathbf d)\ge m(1-\epsilon)/2$.

title: Proof
body_md: Here $\lfloor d_\ell/q_\ell\rfloor=1$ and $m(1-\epsilon)/2=3$, and $t_{\mathfrak q}=\frac35\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a}(P)$ with $\mathbf a=(\sqrt2,\dots,\sqrt2)$. The condition therefore forces $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf a}(P)\ge5$. As $P$ has rational coefficients, conjugation gives $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbf b}(P)\ge5$ at $\mathbf b=-\mathbf a$, contradicting Lemma~\ref{lem:twopoints}.
